newsitem.title: ITALY: Tunisia's Ben Ali attacks Israel over settlements.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia's Ben Ali attacks Israel over settlements.

text.p: Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali said on Wednesday that Israel's settlement policy was threatening Middle East peace.
In an address during a state dinner at Italy's Quirinale presidential palace on the first day of a visit to Rome, the president also called for an end to current embargoes against Libya and Iraq.
In the speech, he attacked what he called Israeli "intransigence" and said there was a "risk of a return of confrontation and armed conflict in the region".
Ben Ali accused Israel of "going ahead with its population policy and not respecting commitments made in the framework of the peace accords".
He called on the international community to assure that accords between the Palestinian Authority and Israel were applied.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud-led government angered Palestinians this year when it lifted a four-year freeze on Jewish settlement construction imposed by the previous left-centre coalition in the West Bank and Gaza.
In March, Netanyahu broke ground for the Jewish settlement of Har Homa on an Arab East Jerusalem hilltop known to Palestinians as Jabal Abu Ghneim.
Ben Ali is due to hold talks on Thursday with Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
